questions.stem: This anterior view of the great vessels shows the aortic arch and its branches. Based on the branching pattern illustrated, how do the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries arise relative to the arch?

choices.label: A
choices.text: They share a common left brachiocephalic trunk

choices.label: B
choices.text: They both branch from a single brachiocephalic trunk with the carotids

choices.label: C
choices.text: They branch from the pulmonary trunk

choices.label: D
choices.text: They arise from the descending thoracic aorta

choices.label: E
choices.text: They arise separately and independently from the arch

explanation.summary: On the left, the common carotid and subclavian arteries arise separately and directly from the aortic arch, unlike the right side where a brachiocephalic trunk first divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. This asymmetry reflects the differing embryologic remodeling of the aortic arches.
explanation.whyCorrect: On the left, the common carotid and subclavian arteries arise separately and directly from the aortic arch, unlike the right side where a brachiocephalic trunk first divides into the right subclavian and right common carotid arteries. This asymmetry reflects the differing embryologic remodeling of the aortic arches.

questions.stem: This lateral view of an early embryo shows a series of ridges labeled as pharyngeal arches. The major arteries and connective/muscular structures derived from these arches ultimately supply which body region?

choices.label: E
choices.text: The lower back and vertebral column

explanation.summary: The pharyngeal (branchial) arches shown remodel to form the great arteries and other structures of the head, neck, and thorax. Somites, the heart bulge, lens placode, and otic placode are also visible, marking key landmarks of the developing embryo.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pharyngeal (branchial) arches shown remodel to form the great arteries and other structures of the head, neck, and thorax. Somites, the heart bulge, lens placode, and otic placode are also visible, marking key landmarks of the developing embryo.

questions.stem: This schematic traces the stepwise remodeling of the paired embryonic aortic arches into the adult great vessels. The distal segment of the left sixth arch that persists rather than regressing becomes which structure?

explanation.summary: The sixth aortic arches give rise to the pulmonary arteries; on the left, the distal segment persists as the ductus arteriosus, whereas on the right this distal portion regresses. This asymmetry also explains the differing courses of the right and left recurrent laryngeal nerves.
